cases.task: Build a day-by-day itinerary for Lake George, NY for Thanksgiving week, November 26–28, 2026, for a group of six adults.

specialist.summary: A Thanksgiving weekend at Lake George features scenic steamboat cruises, lake kayaking, casual mini-golf, and dining at local Italian and Japanese restaurants, with optional whitewater rafting on Saturday.

stops.title: Lake George Steamboat Company
stops.description: Take a scenic cruise on one of the authentic passenger vessels operated by this historic company, founded in 1817. The steamboat offers views of the lake and surrounding landscape. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Mario's Restaurant
stops.description: This restaurant has been serving Italian cuisine since 1954 and offers a full-service bar. Dinner is offered M-Th from 4:30PM; reservations are advised. Confirm it's open on Thanksgiving. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: Lake George Kayak Company
stops.description: Rent kayaks and paddle on Lake George. This is a great way to get out on your own and check out the lake. Be prepared for the weather and watch out for wind direction as it can affect your paddling back to shore. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Gooney Golf
stops.description: A typical old-fashioned mini-golf with classic windmill-type obstacles. This is a fun group activity. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Sushi Yoshi
stops.description: This hibachi steakhouse serves Chinese and Japanese food with authentic low tables situated over hollow pits, allowing guests to dine in Japanese izakaya style. Lunch and dinner seven days a week. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

cases.task: Build a day-by-day itinerary for Savannah, GA, April 9–11, 2027, for two adults who like history and food.

specialist.summary: A three-day Savannah itinerary blending history and food: explore the historic district and riverside, visit historic sites like Wormsloe and Bonaventure Cemetery, and dine at local favorites from fine Italian at Saint Bibiana to Southern classics at Desposito's shrimp shack.

stops.title: Gallery Espresso
stops.description: Start your day with coffee and pastries at this arty coffee shop with outside seating on Chippewa Square. They offer a large menu of coffees, teas, sweets and sandwiches. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: River Street
stops.description: Explore the cobblestone streets of Savannah's Historic District and walk along River Street on the south bank of the Savannah River. The area is lined with numerous shops and restaurants, and features the sculpture of the Waving Girl towards the east end.

stops.title: Forsyth Park
stops.description: Visit this large public park that marks the southern edge of the Historic District, crowned with a beautiful fountain and ringed with Spanish moss. This is the filming location of Midnight in the Garden of Good & Evil. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: City Market
stops.description: Explore this mixed-use development in the northwest corner of the Historic District, a four-block area rehabilitated beginning in 1985. It features shops, galleries, and dining venues. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Saint Bibiana
stops.description: A fine Italian cuisine restaurant and cocktail lounge located in the restored 1888 Savannah Mansion at the Savannah Bardo Hotel, adorned with chic artwork and stunning chandeliering. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: Wormsloe Historic Site
stops.description: Visit this historic plantation with a beautiful avenue of live oak trees at the entrance and a visitor's center showcasing the plantation's history. Explore trails along the marshes. Hours: Daily 9AM–5PM. Cost: $10 per adult. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Bonaventure Cemetery
stops.description: Explore this atmospheric cemetery where fans of 'The Book' can find Johnny Mercer's grave, along with those of Conrad Aiken and other Southern notables. The view of the river is wonderful, and Spanish moss creates a delightfully spooky atmosphere. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Georgia State Railroad Museum
stops.description: Tour this museum featuring several vintage pieces of rolling stock, an operating model train layout, and an operating turntable. Hours: Daily 9AM–5PM. Cost: $7.70 for adults. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: B&D Burgers
stops.description: Local chain with excellent burgers. Multiple downtown locations available, including off Ellis Square and further west on Broughton. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: The Collins Quarter at Forsyth
stops.description: Enjoy brunch at the only restaurant inside Forsyth Park with a great brunch menu and pleasant atmosphere. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: Savannah College of Art & Design
stops.description: Walk through the campus of this independent art and design school founded in 1978, known for its impact on Savannah's cultural landscape and its support of the Lucas Theatre and film festival. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Plant Riverside District
stops.description: Explore this recently redeveloped former power plant that opened in 2020, featuring the J. W. Marriott hotel's publicly-accessible Generator Hall with shops, restaurants, and a large collection of minerals and geodes on display.

stops.title: Desposito's
stops.description: One of the few surviving family-owned shrimp shacks from a previous era, featuring their secret-recipe dipping sauce used for more than half a century. Go for a taste of old-timey Southern boiled shrimp. Hours: Tue–Sat 5–10PM. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

cases.task: Build a two-day itinerary for Harpers Ferry, WV, November 14–15, 2026, for two adults.

specialist.summary: A two-day itinerary exploring Harpers Ferry's Civil War and abolitionist history, with visits to the Lower Town historic district, John Brown's Fort, battlefield walks, and scenic river viewpoints.

stops.title: Visitor Center orientation and shuttle to Lower Town
stops.description: Start your visit at the Visitor Center to orient yourself and understand the historical significance of Harpers Ferry. Take the shuttle to Lower Town, the historic heart of the site where you can begin exploring the preserved buildings and streets.

stops.title: Lower Town historic district and John Brown's Fort
stops.description: Explore the Lower Town historic district, a preserved community that showcases life during the 1800s. Visit John Brown's Fort, where the abolitionist John Brown made his famous raid in 1859. This is the central cultural landmark of Harpers Ferry National Historical Park.

stops.title: The Point river-confluence viewpoint
stops.description: Head to The Point to experience the scenic confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers at sunset. This outdoor viewpoint offers perspective on the geography that made Harpers Ferry strategically important throughout American history.

stops.title: Bolivar Heights battlefield walk
stops.description: Spend your morning walking the Bolivar Heights battlefield, where significant Civil War engagements took place. This outdoor cultural site offers insight into the military history of the region and beautiful views of the surrounding landscape.

sources.title: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park Planning Guide

cases.task: Build a day-by-day itinerary for San Juan, Puerto Rico, December 4–6, 2026, for two adults.

specialist.summary: Your 3-day San Juan itinerary (Dec 4–6, 2026) features historic sites like Castillo San Cristóbal and Casa Blanca, cultural experiences including a bioluminescent bay kayak and Old San Juan walking tour, and meals at local restaurants ranging from casual Puerto Rican fare to upscale dining, with typical December weather around 84°F highs and 73°F lows.

stops.title: San Juan National Historic Site
stops.description: One of the largest Spanish fortresses in the New World. The National Park Service visitor center is located off Avenida Luis Muñoz Rivera and offers English and Spanish introductions to the site. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: La Casa del Libro
stops.description: Museum of rare books and manuscripts spanning five centuries, with nearly 5,000 early works including pieces from the 15th century and two royal mandates signed by Ferdinand and Isabella. Located at 255 Calle del Cristo. Hours: Tue–Fri 11AM–5PM, Sat 11:30AM–5:30PM. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: El Asador, The Grill Old San Juan
stops.description: Puerto Rican cuisine at the entrance of Old San Juan, featuring a two-level restaurant with an exterior patio. Hours: Daily 10AM–4AM. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: Bioluminescent bay kayak (Fajardo)
stops.description: Paddling tour through a bioilluminescent bay. This is a unique natural phenomenon accessible by excursion from San Juan.

stops.title: Casa Blanca
stops.description: Ancestral home of the Ponce de Leon family, now a museum located at the western end of Calle San Sebastián. Hours: Wed–Sun 8:30AM–noon and 1:30–4PM. Price: $5 adults, $3 seniors/students/children. Confirm it's open on your dates.

stops.title: Ostra Cosa
stops.description: Upscale dining with sensual and romantic ambience in Old San Juan. Reservations recommended. Hours: Daily noon–10PM. Located at Calle del Cristo 154. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)

stops.title: Condado beach day
stops.description: Relax and swim at one of San Juan's popular beaches in the Condado neighborhood.

stops.title: Old San Juan walking tour
stops.description: Guided cultural walking tour through historic Old San Juan, including cobblestone streets and colorful colonial architecture.

stops.title: La Bombonera
stops.description: Authentic local cuisine in a landmark atmosphere unchanged for decades, serving lunch and dinner. Fresh pastries, superlative coffee, and inexpensive prices. Hours: 7:30AM–8PM. Located at 259 Viejo, C. de San Francisco. (Wikivoyage listing; confirm hours)
